hook.line: At three in the morning, staring at Altamira's offer, Tomás finally gets an idea. In Spanish the idea does the arriving: it turns up *to* you, and you are just the person it reaches.

examples.es: Se me ocurrió una solución mientras dormía.
examples.en: A solution came to me while I was sleeping.
It didn't occur to me to call you.
How can you even think of saying that? (to a friend)

examples.es: A Vale se le ocurrió cambiar el menú.
examples.en: It occurred to Vale to change the menu.
Can you think of another option? (to a friend)

rule:
The idea is the subject, and you are the person it happens to. Build it in three pieces: *se*, then *me / te / le / nos / les*, then *ocurre* or *ocurrió*.

*Se me ocurrió una idea*: an idea occurred to me. If what occurs is plural, the verb is plural: *se nos ocurrieron dos ideas*. You can follow it with an infinitive: *No se me ocurrió llamarte*.

English says "I had an idea". Spanish does not say *yo ocurrí*. And *¿Cómo se te ocurre…?* is not a real question: it is a reproach, "how can you even think of…".
smallPrint: Teachers call this a *se* construction for things that happen to you: the thing is the subject, the person is an indirect object.

options: An idea occurred to me.
An idea occurred to you.
An idea occurred to him.
One idea occurred to me.
Two ideas occurred to us.
Two ideas occurred to me.

readAndPick.es: Se nos ocurrió llamar a Hernando.
options: It occurred to me to call Hernando.
It occurred to us to call Hernando.
It occurred to them to call Hernando.
How can he even think of saying that?
How do I come up with that?
How can you even think of saying that?
Nothing occurred to him.
Nothing occurred to me.
Something occurred to me.
A solution occurred to us.
A solution occurred to her.
A solution occurred to them.
Can you think of another option?
Can I think of another option?
Can she think of another option?

readAndPick.es: No se le ocurrió abrir más temprano.
options: It occurred to him to open earlier.
It didn't occur to him to open earlier.
It didn't occur to us to open earlier.

yourTurn.prompt: An idea occurred to me. Fill the gap: ___ una idea. (*me ocurrió* or *se me ocurrió*)
yourTurn.why: The idea is what arrives, so *se* comes first and *me* says who it reached.

yourTurn.prompt: It didn't occur to me to call you. (*tú*)
yourTurn.why: Put *no* before the whole *se me ocurrió* block.
The verb agrees with the ideas (two), and *nos* says who they reached.

yourTurn.prompt: It occurred to Vale to change the menu.
yourTurn.answer: A Vale se le ocurrió cambiar el menú.
accept: Se le ocurrió a Vale cambiar el menú.
yourTurn.why: *Le* stands for Vale, and *a Vale* says who it is.

yourTurn.prompt: Reproach a friend: how can you even think of saying that?
yourTurn.why: *Se te ocurre* turns the question into a protest.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural, about two ideas: *Se me ocurrió una idea.*
yourTurn.why: Two ideas arrive, so the verb takes the plural ending.

yourTurn.prompt: Can you think of another option? (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Te* is the friend the idea would reach.

pitfalls.why: Almost. The idea is what happens; you are the one it happens to.
The verb agrees with the ideas, not with you.
Without *se*, *ocurrir* just means "to happen". Keep the *se*.

personal: Say one thing that never occurred to you until it was too late. Start with *No se me ocurrió…*
